comment: Ep81 Ivory Coast vs Norway (R32). lines.text: In the old Norse tales there is a wolf so vast the gods themselves feared him — Fenrir, bound in a magic chain, fated to break loose and swallow the world. Tonight, the chain is slipping.
And out of the golden savanna comes the Elephant — sacred, immense, impossible to move. Ivory Coast, the land of champions. The wolf meets the elephant.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends — episode eighty-one. Ivory Coast, versus Norway. A knockout. Win, or the dark takes you.
Ivory Coast arrive as champions of Africa — the proud Elephants, the land of Drogba. Norway arrive as the wolf generation: hungry, fearless, led by a monster up front.
Ivory Coast — Les Éléphants. Powerful, fast, fearless. A team that conquered a continent and now wants the world.
Nicolas Pépé glides in off the right with that wicked left foot. Sébastien Haller leads the line, a striker reborn. And Franck Kessié drives the engine from deep, all muscle and will.
Wilfried Singo storms up the wing like a force of nature. And Simon Adingra dances past defenders as if they aren't there.
Norway — the wolves of the north. Cold, clinical, and carried by two of the finest players on the planet.
Erling Haaland is the monster up front — a force of pure violence in the box. Martin Ødegaard, the captain, conducts it all with silk. And Alexander Sørloth gives them a second giant.
Antonio Nusa runs at you with fearless young legs. And Sander Berge holds the middle like a wall of ice.
So here is the riddle. Can the Elephant stand immovable against the wolf? Or does Fenrir slip the chain and devour another giant?
And stay with me — because this one turns, late, on the jaws of a single man.
Here is how we see it. Ivory Coast come out roaring — Adingra flying, Singo storming — and Norway are rocked back on their heels.
The Elephants smell blood. The savanna shakes with orange.
And it lands. Sébastien Haller pounces in the box and finishes ice-cold. Ivory Coast lead. The Elephant stands tall.
But you cannot keep a wolf chained forever. Norway stir. Ødegaard begins to pull the strings, and the monster up front starts to growl.
And Erling Haaland erupts. He bullies his way through and smashes it home. One — one. The wolf is loose.
And then, late, the jaws close. Haaland strikes again — clinical, merciless, a second goal from nothing. Two — one, Norway. Fenrir devours another giant.
Two — one. The Elephant stood proud and tall — but the wolf was simply too hungry, too cold, too good. The chain is broken.
Our prediction — Norway two, Ivory Coast one. Haaland, a brace, late. Not played yet — the real ninety is yours to watch.
And Ivory Coast leave with heads high — the Elephants fell to no ordinary team, but to the hungriest wolf in the world.
Norway march on. The wolves of the north, reminding everyone that when Fenrir slips the chain, no giant is safe.
So you tell me — the Elephant, or the wolf? Comment IVORY COAST for the Elephants — comment NORWAY for the wolves of the north.

In the frozen north they whisper of Fenrir — the great wolf the gods could not kill, only bind, knowing that one day the chain would break and the old order would end. Legend eighty-one — Fenrir, the Unbound Wolf.
The players write the night. But Fenrir carries one truth — what you chain out of fear does not vanish. It only grows hungrier in the dark.
